qAndA.question: What is the peak wavelength of the Sun?

qAndA.answer: The Earth's atmosphere absorbs shorter wavelengths like blue and green, leaving more red and yellow wavelengths visible when the Sun is low in the sky.
qAndA.question: Why does the Sun appear yellow or red at sunrise and sunset?
What color would the Sun appear to an observer in space?
What type of light does the Sun emit the most of?

narrativeProgression.description: Robert Wagner introduces the misconception that the Sun is yellow, supported by common images.
He debunks the misconception, explaining the Sun emits all visible colors, with the peak wavelength falling in the green spectrum. However, the combination of colors makes it appear white from space.
He further explains the role of Earth's atmosphere in making the Sun appear yellow, orange, or red due to the absorption of shorter wavelengths. He highlights this phenomenon at sunrise and sunset.
Robert Wagner reiterates that the Sun is too bright to be looked at directly and emphasizes how the atmosphere impacts the perceived color.
He summarizes that the Sun emits a range of wavelengths in the visible spectrum, with a peak in green light, but the overall effect is white light.

youtube_description:
In this lecture, we will look at the color of the Sun. We will discuss in what color the Sun actually emits more light and how Earth's atmosphere affects how we see the Sun.

The Astronomy Picture of the Day video will be uploaded each Monday.
The Misconception in Astronomy video will be uploaded each Wednesday.
The Special Topic in Astronomy video will be uploaded each Friday.

These lecture videos are designed to complement the content in the OpenStax Astronomy 2e textbook. The book can be downloaded free of charge at: https://openstax.org/details/books/astronomy-2e

I can be reached with comments at wagnerastronomy@gmail.com. However, classes I am teaching receive priority so I will try to respond as I can to questions.

Note: Lesson 0 materials are specific for the classes that I teach. Lesson 1 will start with Chapter 1 of the textbook.

You can access the most current versions of the lecture videos through the following playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLMahwAGxKuWlWcYdu2hPMmcD_pyQWkZ7J

The series on Misconceptions in Astronomy is available here: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLMahwAGxKuWlnx5g7C9QD9imNQ-838WzF

The series on Special Topics in Astronomy is available here: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLMahwAGxKuWmpPh2U_DXAqGPeVl_tjudf

These videos are being released under a CC-BY license so that others can feel free to adapt them for their use as long as attribution is given. 

Lecture slides are available for download here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/12JnRLzV-o4xl5KnJ39bGyK27qG7s0Lnw?usp=sharing They are currently available in Apple Keynote, PowerPoint, and pdf format.
